ddl:
CREATE TABLE Book_Category (
    Book_Type_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Description VARCHAR(255),
    Type_Name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Reader_Category (
    Description VARCHAR(255),
    Reader_Type_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Type_Name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Book (
    Author VARCHAR(255),
    Book_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Book_Type_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Content_Description VARCHAR(255),
    Price FLOAT,
    Publication_Date DATETIME,
    Publisher VARCHAR(255),
    Title VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (Book_Type_ID) REFERENCES Book_Category(Book_Type_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Reader (
    Contact_Number INTEGER,
    Credit_Score FLOAT,
    Description VARCHAR(255),
    Reader_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Reader_Type_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (Reader_Type_ID) REFERENCES Reader_Category(Reader_Type_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Borrowing_Information (
    Book_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Borrow_Date DATETIME,
    Fine FLOAT,
    Reader_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Renewal_Count VARCHAR(255),
    Return_Date DATETIME,
    PRIMARY KEY (Book_ID, Reader_ID, Borrow_Date),
    FOREIGN KEY (Book_ID) REFERENCES Book(Book_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Reader_ID) REFERENCES Reader(Reader_ID)
);
gold_question:
The library management system is as follows:
The library has multiple books, each book has a Book ID, Title, Author, Publisher, Publication Date, Price, Book Type, and Content Description.     
Book Type information is stored in the Book Category table, which includes Book Type ID, Type Name, and Description.
The library has multiple readers, each reader has a Reader ID, Reader Type, Contact Number, Credit Score, and Description.
Reader Type information is stored in the Reader Category table, which includes Reader Type ID, Type Name, and Description.
The borrowing process is recorded in the Borrowing table, each borrowing record has a Book ID, Reader ID, Borrow Date, Return Date, Renewal Count, and Fine.
The system manages book borrowing and returning, as well as reader borrowing permissions and credit scores through this information.
